messages:
sam_support: Heads-up: MercuryPay reporting huge p95 jump and throughput drop after last weekend deploy. They say median ok but p95 ~2.8s -> 3.5s for chat completions and sustained 40% lower qps. Raising for intake.
arun_sales: This is a Dedicated customer on reserved pool (eu-west). They flagged SLA risk and sales is asking for an ETA. They have a big payments deadline next month.
jess_product: Thanks. Can you paste the customer's timestamps and an example request? Also what's their plan if we can't fix quickly (rollback / routing)? We need severity and ask whether to escalate to P1.
sam_support: Example curl and payload below; timestamps from their observation window (UTC): 2026-03-08T07:12:11Z -> 2026-03-08T08:02:00Z. Attached minimal input: `curl -X POST /v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-1.5b","prompt":"analyze tx logs"}'` . They saw p95 jump starting 2026-03-08T07:18Z.
maria_eng_runtime: Quick triage checklist: 1) model variant pinned? 2) KV cache hit rate change? 3) batcher queue depth + avg batch size 4) routing fallbacks triggered? 5) GPU util / stalls. Can someone grab those metrics for the 07:00-08:15 window?
lee_oncall: Pasted some snippets from observability (trimmed): ```
# metrics
batcher.queue_depth: 0.0 -> spiked to 350 at 07:18
avg_batch_size: 1.3 -> 1.1
kv_cache.hit_rate: 0.82 -> 0.47
serve.latency.p95: 0.95s -> 3.48s
gpu.util: stable 68% -> 72%
# logs
2026-03-08T07:18:02Z runner: backpressure applied, drop_rate=0.12
2026-03-08T07:18:12Z fallback_router: routed 18% -> 5% (less fallback than expected)
``` 
lee_oncall: Looks like a KV cache regression + batcher queueing. Not pure GPU saturation.
arun_sales: If KV cache hit rate dropped, could be cached key eviction after quantized model swap? They did request a model bump last week.
jess_product: OK, product decision: prioritize as P1 customer-impacting regression. Immediate scope: mitigation (routing to previous model variant or increase cache TTLs), triage action items, and a post-fix rollout plan. Launch criteria for permanent fix: p95 within 15% of baseline for 48h and no QoS violations. Anyone object?
maria_eng_runtime: No objections. Proposed short actions: 1) roll routing of MercuryPay traffic to redwood-1.4b-quant until root cause; 2) revert the model-specific cache eviction policy change that landed in release/2026-03-07; 3) add KV cache hit-rate alert at 10% delta. I can own 1+2, need ops help for rollout.
opsbot: deploybot: release/checks -> release/2026-03-07 (model-cache-change) shows approved. Can rollback with `deploy rollback release/2026-03-07 --target mercurypay-dedicated` (requires ops approval).
sam_support: MercuryPay agreed to routing to older variant if it reduces latency. They asked for ETA ASAP.
arun_sales: Sales note: offer 10% credit if not fixed within 72h. Need ETA to commit.
jess_product: Maria + Ops: can you aim to have routing change and cache revert staged in the next 2 hours and validated on canary? If yes we'll tell sales/customer. Add risk notes and rollback plan. I'll create a backlog ticket with severity P1 and acceptance criteria (p95 < baseline*1.15 for 48h, no error rate regression). Also flag for postmortem in #postmortems if we don't hit criteria.
maria_eng_runtime: Ack. Starting canary now. I will post canary results in this thread within 45m.
lee_oncall: Monitoring: I'll keep an eye on batcher queue and KV hit rate and post alerts. If queue_depth > 50 for 5m -> page.
jess_product: Thanks team. Recording owners: maria_eng_runtime (fix & rollback), lee_oncall (monitoring), sam_support (customer comms), arun_sales (contract/credits). Moving to active intake board and assigning ticket PROD-4682. If anything blocks deployment ping me directly.
opsbot: deploybot: rollback job queued for mercurypay-dedicated by maria_eng_runtime. Job id: db-job-8842.
sam_support: Noted, I'll inform MercuryPay of planned routing within 30m.
maria_eng_runtime: Canary now shows kv_cache.hit_rate back to 0.79 and p95 down to 1.02s on canary slice. Rolling to full dedicated pool.
jess_product: Great. Keep this thread updated; if stable for 24h we'll close intake and move to retrospective. If regression persists we'll open a deep-dive in #eng-runtime and schedule postmortem.
